title: An email with your news
subtitle: What has changed since you last wrote
goal: You can write an email with your news: react to what your friend wrote, give two or three pieces of your own news with details, and ask questions back.
why: This is the email everybody writes and almost nobody answers well: the news arrives without dates, without details and without a single question in return.
example: Aigerim answered a pen-friend point by point and asked two questions. The reply came the same evening — the first time in four months.
writeTask: Write an email with your news (80–110 words): thank your friend for their letter, react to one thing they wrote, give two pieces of your own news with details, ask two questions and close warmly.

tasks.title: Build the sentence
tasks.howto: Tap the words in the right order — they move into the line. Tap a word in the line to send it back. English word order is fixed, so the order itself carries the meaning.

items.src: I started this course in September and I am still doing it.
answers: I have been doing this course since September.
I have done this course since September.
items.why: An action that started in the past and continues now takes Present Perfect.

items.src: Somebody stole my bike last week.
answers: My bike was stolen last week.
items.why: When the person is unknown, English moves the object to the front.

items.cue: Join the two sentences with although
items.src: The test was difficult. I passed it.
answers: Although the test was difficult, I passed it.
items.why: Although turns two facts into one sentence with a clear relationship.

items.cue: Add a reason with because of
items.src: The trip was cancelled. The weather was bad.
answers: The trip was cancelled because of the bad weather.
items.why: Because of is followed by a noun phrase, not by a full clause.

items.src: I need info about the course.
answers: I would like some information about the course.
items.why: Info is a spoken abbreviation and information is uncountable.

items.src: It is a good idea to arrive early.
items.why: Should is the standard way to give advice in English.

items.src: This café is cheap. That café is not cheap.
answers: This café is cheaper than that one.
items.why: A comparison needs the comparative form plus than.

items.cue: Use going to for a plan
items.src: My plan is to study medicine.
answers: I am going to study medicine.
items.why: Going to is for decisions you have already made.

items.a: Sorry about the noise on Saturday evening.

items.a: I regret that I am unable to come.

items.a: The jacket arrived with a broken zip.
